title: Imaging Supermassive Black Holes
excerpt: The astrophysics of Very Long Baseline Interferometry, synchronizing millimeter radiotelescopes across planet Earth to resolve event horizon shadow structures.
author: Dr. Zachary Vance
imageAlt: Starfield cosmos with glowing gravitational accretion disk around a celestial singularity

body.text: Resolving the event horizon of Messier 87 or Sagittarius A* is equivalent to spotting an orange on the surface of the Moon from Earth. No single optical telescope could ever achieve the angular resolution required. The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) achieves this by combining synchronized radio observatories across six continents into a virtual telescope as large as our planet.

items: Hydrogen Maser Atomic Clocks: Providing ultra-stable sub-picosecond timing precision to tag petabytes of raw astronomical wavefront data.
1.3-Millimeter Atmospheric Transparency: Tuning receivers to 230 GHz to pierce through galactic synchrotron dust and Earth moisture clouds.
Supercomputer Data Correlation: Processing hard drives shipped from Antarctica and Atacama through specialized ASIC correlation supercomputers.
Computational Interferometric Imaging: Utilizing sparse Bayesian modeling and neural networks to reconstruct images from incomplete Fourier baseline coverage.

body.text: We turned planet Earth into a single cosmic magnifying glass to test Einstein’s general relativity at the ultimate boundary of spacetime.

body.text: The resulting shadow images directly confirm the photon ring geometry predicted by Einstein's field equations for a spinning Kerr black hole, demonstrating relativistic Doppler beaming along the approaching accretion plasma flow.
